newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania average one-week rate jumps to 90 pct.
newsitem.headline: Romania average one-week rate jumps to 90 pct.

text.p: The average rate on Romania's central bank's one-week funds surged to 90 percent at Thursday's refinancing auction from 81 percent last week, central bank (BNR) data showed.
The BNR offer of 600 billion lei, slightly up from 550 billion lei previously, was heavily oversubscribed, with three banks bidding a total 1.222 trillion lei.
Traders said banks had rushed to "take a bite" from the BNR offer as the money market was dried up of leu funds. The three banks entered bids at prices ranging from 86 percent to 90 percent.
Interbank short-term rates, which hovered near 80 percent, are expected to climb following the rate hike.
Traders said the rate rise would make Romanian floating-rate treasury bills more attractive as the calculation of their annual yield is based on the average one-week rate.

On Thursday, in a bid to calm down inflation and prop up a depreciating leu currency, the BNR tightened again its monetary policies by lifting its minimum permitted rate to 85 percent from a previous 80 percent.
The leu has slipped by some 50 percent to 6,150/200 against the dollar since January 1.
Year-on-year inflation was 56.9 percent last December, almost three times the IMF-agreed 20 percent target for 1996.
The other BNR key rates, the discount and the Lombard rate, stayed unchanged at an annual 50 percent and 90 respectively.
An IMF mission is now in Bucharest to discuss a new loan arrangement for Romania with the centrist coalition government which emerged from general elections last November.
The Fund credits to Romania were suspended last year because of foreign exchange market curbs and overspending by the former leftist government.
